body:
SLICE 2a DONE (built, not walked): PR #77, the server's janitor `ref_janitor.py` (B-131 server half, B-126 clean-up). One more hourly errand of the library link, after the finders; 500 refs a pass; a ref goes when nothing of anybody points at it, it has no live N-13 verdict, it NEVER held a file (no file_log row) and it is older than 14 days; no migration, file_log never touched.
DECISIONS beyond the design notes: `instr` instead of LIKE; only QUEUED/RUNNING work counts (finished rows stay in the table and would make every ref immortal); change_log is not a pointer and its rows stay (the feed says `removed`, tested); the live-verdict test is in SQL built from missing's own constants and walked against standing_of at every boundary.
THE ADVISOR'S REVIEW CHANGED ONE THING (the rule above): the first version deleted the file_log rows of retired refs and kept a ref whose files changed in the last 14 days. WRONG: a phone that was away learns that a song's file is gone only from the files feed, which lists a ref that STILL EXISTS with `file: null` (`library.files_since` skips a ref that is gone; the phone's `dropUnused` then clears the row). Retiring a ref that once held a file leaves an away phone with a playable-looking song for ever. So `file_history` keeps any ref with a file_log row, with no age bound; a test proves an away phone is still told. COST: refs whose file was removed stay (as today), bounded by the number of files ever removed; the junk the janitor is for (taps, typing) never had a file.
GUARDS for later: every table that names a ref must be classified in `ref_janitor` (CI fails otherwise); each clause is shown load-bearing; no pointer table is scanned; the pass is atomic across statements.
STILL TO DO. SLICE 2b (the phone): a library row with is_ref, no file, like, playlist entry, download or play, absent from every feed page, older than 14 days is dropped by the pass that already drops unused rows; never a row the person is looking at; its own age rule, do not widen the feed. Two edges for 2b, both a clean typed error today (`NotFoundFailure(unknownRef)` from a 404 `not_found`), not a crash: (1) an outbox edit naming a ref resolved more than 14 days earlier, sent after more than 14 days offline; (2) a download that FAILED (its work item is `failed`, which is not a pointer, and there is no index on work_item(ref) to count recent failures) and is retried after the ref was retired: the retry says "That song is not known to this server." SLICE 2c (REMOVAL TRIGGER of the file_history clause): a files-feed tombstone (the feed says "gone" for a retired ref; a FEATURE STRING in info, because an old phone parses every `refs` entry as a full ref; the phone reads it), after which refs that once held a file can be retired too. N-27 must NOT be marked built until 2b and 2c are done, or 2c is split into its own board item.
BENCH CHECK OWED (nothing walked): on VM 108 count song_ref rows before and after one hourly pass with an old junk ref present. Merge order: P2-12 slice 1 also edits errands() in api.py: the second to land merges main by hand and keeps BOTH errands.
